answer: A scripted farm therefore has to pad 285 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is recorded against the wharf challenge, the bridge audit can replay the haven history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A farm of 774 identities would post 1754 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
